_comment: WORKED EXAMPLE — Stages 2-3 output for the fictional Acme RFP. Every content block carries either non-empty sources (knowledge-bank entry IDs) or gap:true. Section slide counts are sized by evaluation weight.
engagement_title: Change Management Partner — Group ERP Replacement

slides.title: Change Management Partner

blocks.content: Change Management Partner — Group ERP Replacement
A phased change partnership for the S/4HANA consolidation across six countries and 4,200 users.
RFP reference ACM-2026-114  ·  Submission due 4 September 2026  ·  DRAFT FOR PRACTITIONER REVIEW

slides.speaker_notes: Check the legal entity name and RFP reference against the RFP cover page before submission.

slides.title: What this programme is really asking of Acme

content: Three regional ERP instances reach end of vendor support in 2028
Group finance cannot close month-end without manual reconciliation
A 2023 consolidation attempt was halted after nine months
Plant managers report fatigue from three concurrent programmes

blocks.content: What that means for the change work

content: The technical case is settled; the adaptive work is at plant level, where the last attempt lost credibility
Scepticism is concentrated, not uniform — engagement spend should follow it rather than spread evenly
With no standing change capability in the Transformation Office, capability transfer is part of the deliverable, not an afterthought
Change fatigue caps how much can be asked in any one quarter; the plan has to be sequenced around it

slides.speaker_notes: Highest-signal slide for 'did they read the RFP'. Every point on the left is traceable to the RFP or the briefing call.

blocks.content: Four phases running alongside the technical delivery plan, so change activity lands before the system does.

slides.title: Four phases, each gated on the last

blocks.content: Each phase's output is the next phase's input — the impact assessment scopes the training needs analysis, which scopes delivery.

content.label: Phase 1
content.name: Assess
detail: Change impact assessment by business unit

slides.speaker_notes: Answers R1 (impact assessment in Assess) and R2 (training in Build/Conduct).

slides.title: Stakeholder engagement: networks, not cascades

content: Network mapping to surface informal influencers — the people the plant actually listens to, who rarely match the org chart
Sentiment captured per group, so engagement effort follows resistance rather than headcount
Explicit read on the two markets where the 2023 attempt lost most credibility
A volunteer change-agent network recruited from the affected population, not appointed regional leads
Participative design sessions where the process genuinely changes; briefings where it does not
A comms calendar synchronised to the technical release plan, so messages land against real milestones

slides.speaker_notes: Answers R3, including its specific ask about informal influencers.

slides.title: Named adoption measures, baselined before go-live

blocks.content: Measures are defined during Assess and baselined before go-live, so the programme can tell adoption from compliance.

rows: Proportion trained by business unit, against plan
Transactions in the new system vs. workarounds
Three-question pulse across the affected population

slides.speaker_notes: Answers R4. A flat or rising proficiency curve four weeks post go-live indicates a training gap, not a system defect.

slides.title: Sustaining the change after we leave

content: Every change artifact has a named Acme business owner from the outset — handover is a phase-gated deliverable, not a closing activity
The change-agent network is recruited and trained as an Acme asset, and persists past the engagement
Capability transfer into the Group Transformation Office is scoped as a deliverable, given there is no standing change capability today
A structured delivery-risk score at each phase gate, so the trend is visible to the board across the engagement

slides.speaker_notes: Answers R8, which is scored under 'sustainability of the change beyond the engagement' but not scoped — see the open question in the brief.

slides.title: Multi-country HRIS rollout after two failed attempts

blocks.content: A multinational manufacturer replacing three regional systems across 5,000 employees in eleven countries. Two prior attempts had stalled, and local teams regarded the programme as a headcount exercise.

content: Ran the impact assessment at country level, which showed resistance was concentrated in two markets rather than spread evenly
Redirected engagement budget accordingly — deep participative design in those two, lighter-touch comms elsewhere
Built a change-agent network of 40 local volunteers instead of appointing regional leads

blocks.content: Both previously-resistant markets finished above the global average. Support ticket volume peaked at half the level forecast from the earlier attempt.

content.label: adoption within 90 days, against a 75% target

slides.title: Phased fee structure

blocks.content: Phased with a commercial break at each gate, so Acme can stop, resize or extend at a known point. Assess is fixed-price on a defined deliverable set; Build and Conduct are capped time-and-materials against an agreed resourcing profile.

rows: Fixed price on a defined deliverable set

blocks.gap_note: Fee figures absent: v0.1 does not calculate pricing, and the rate card is held separately and confirmed per bid. R7 is mandatory and requires a fixed price for the assessment phase — this cannot be submitted until the practitioner completes the table above.

slides.speaker_notes: The structure is from the bank; the numbers are deliberately absent. Never generate a fee figure.

slides.title: Assumptions and exclusions

content: A named Acme business sponsor and business-unit champions, with time formally allocated rather than absorbed alongside a full role
Access to affected staff for the impact assessment and training within agreed windows
Client-provided facilities and system environments for training delivery
Travel and expenses at cost against an agreed cap
Technical configuration and data migration
Systems integration testing
Translation of training content into local languages

slides.speaker_notes: Translation is worth flagging to the practitioner — six countries, and the RFP does not say whether local-language delivery is expected.

content: Diagnostic before prescription — the approach is sized to the change in front of us, and a rollout following a halted attempt is not a standard rollout
Networks over hierarchies — engagement runs through volunteers recruited from the affected population, because cascades lose fidelity at every layer
Measurement built in from the start, baselined before go-live, so adoption can be told apart from compliance
Handover as a deliverable — change that depends on the consultants staying is not change, and Acme has no standing change capability to fall back on
